svg.title: $505,000 Earned Fees to $217,150 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-earned-fee-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $505,000 Earned Fees to $217,150 Owner Profit; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 43.0% net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Canonical endpoints are $505,000 annual operator revenue and $217,150 owner profit. Cost splits and the supporting recovery pool are illustrative engineering assumptions. Example fee base: $2,200,000 incremental provider cash collected minus $80,000 unrecovered administrative/entity fees minus $100,000 provider-borne casework costs equals $2,020,000; a 25% retained share produces $505,000 earned operator revenue. Those two provider-borne deductions are outside the operator expense bars and must not be deducted twice. No baseline provider collections are included.; caption: $505,000 − $156,000 − $30,000 − $36,000 − $65,850 = $217,150. Owner profit divided by earned operator revenue equals 43.0%. The first and last bars are totals; the four middle bars are negative changes, not additional revenue.; stages: label: Earned operator revenue; value: $505,000 annual fee revenue; numeric value: 505000.0; detail: Recognize the operator's earned 25% share of the $2,020,000 net incremental collection pool. Where the operator is an agent under ASC 606, exclude provider proceeds and pass-through recoveries from recognized revenue; document the principal-versus-agent assessment.; label: Variable delivery labor; value: −$156,000 annual expense; numeric value: -156000.0; detail: Illustrative operator-funded contractor delivery labor and specialist support, separate from provider-borne casework already deducted in the fee-base calculation. Owner distributions are not a second labor deduction.; label: Systems and protected storage; value: −$30,000 annual expense; numeric value: -30000.0; detail: Budget $2,500 monthly for contracted secure infrastructure, 835 ingestion, access logging, deadline automation, and licensed evidence tools. Verify business-associate terms before any service receives protected health information.; label: Core operating overhead; value: −$36,000 annual expense; numeric value: -36000.0; detail: Budget $3,000 monthly for insurance, accounting, workspace, and routine administration. Combined with systems, $5,500 monthly fixed overhead sits within the supplied $1,800–$10,500 core operating budget range.; label: Acquisition and variable support; value: −$65,850 annual expense; numeric value: -65850.0; detail: Allocate illustrative non-fixed acquisition, provider onboarding, and transaction support costs. Total operator expenses are $287,850 annually; the monthly core budget range does not represent all-in expenses including variable delivery and acquisition.; label: Owner net profit; value: $217,150 at 43.0%; numeric value: 217150.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual residual for the 1 FT + 2 C pod. Preserve the scorecard's owner-profit definition; do not silently recast this figure as a provider recovery amount, salary figure, or award-value margin.

rect.title: label: Earned operator revenue; value: $505,000 annual fee revenue; numeric value: 505000.0; detail: Recognize the operator's earned 25% share of the $2,020,000 net incremental collection pool. Where the operator is an agent under ASC 606, exclude provider proceeds and pass-through recoveries from recognized revenue; document the principal-versus-agent assessment.

label: Variable delivery labor; value: −$156,000 annual expense; numeric value: -156000.0; detail: Illustrative operator-funded contractor delivery labor and specialist support, separate from provider-borne casework already deducted in the fee-base calculation. Owner distributions are not a second labor deduction.

label: Systems and protected storage; value: −$30,000 annual expense; numeric value: -30000.0; detail: Budget $2,500 monthly for contracted secure infrastructure, 835 ingestion, access logging, deadline automation, and licensed evidence tools. Verify business-associate terms before any service receives protected health information.

label: Core operating overhead; value: −$36,000 annual expense; numeric value: -36000.0; detail: Budget $3,000 monthly for insurance, accounting, workspace, and routine administration. Combined with systems, $5,500 monthly fixed overhead sits within the supplied $1,800–$10,500 core operating budget range.

label: Acquisition and variable support; value: −$65,850 annual expense; numeric value: -65850.0; detail: Allocate illustrative non-fixed acquisition, provider onboarding, and transaction support costs. Total operator expenses are $287,850 annually; the monthly core budget range does not represent all-in expenses including variable delivery and acquisition.

label: Owner net profit; value: $217,150 at 43.0%; numeric value: 217150.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual residual for the 1 FT + 2 C pod. Preserve the scorecard's owner-profit definition; do not silently recast this figure as a provider recovery amount, salary figure, or award-value margin.

text.title: Assumptions: Canonical endpoints are $505,000 annual operator revenue and $217,150 owner profit. Cost splits and the supporting recovery pool are illustrative engineering assumptions. Example fee base: $2,200,000 incremental provider cash collected minus $80,000 unrecovered administrative/entity fees minus $100,000 provider-borne casework costs equals $2,020,000; a 25% retained share produces $505,000 earned operator revenue. Those two provider-borne deductions are outside the operator expense bars and must not be deducted twice. No baseline provider collections are included.
